title: Sets of Rational Numbers: Natural, Whole, Integers and Rational
seo_title: Grade 7 Sets of Rational Numbers Worksheets: Venn Diagram (TEKS 7.2, STAAR)
standard_text: 7.2 extend previous knowledge of sets and subsets using a visual representation to describe relationships between sets of rational numbers
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 worksheets for Texas TEKS 7.2: classify natural numbers, whole numbers, integers and rational numbers with a Venn diagram, terminating and repeating decimals. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: 0 is whole but not natural. 0.333… = 1/3 is rational.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Natural numbers (counting numbers): 1, 2, 3, …
  • Whole numbers: 0, 1, 2, 3, …
  • Integers: … −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, …
  • Rational numbers: any number that can be written as a fraction a/b, including terminating and repeating decimals. Each set is inside the next one.

Examples

Example

Classify −7.

Not a counting number or 0

It is the opposite of 7

Answer: integer and rational

Example

Is 0.666… rational?

0.666… = 2/3

Answer: yes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling 0 a natural numberNatural numbers start at 1. 0 is a whole number.
Thinking repeating decimals are not rational0.333… = 1/3, so it is rational.
Calling negative fractions integers−1/2 is rational but not an integer.

faq.a: Extend previous knowledge of sets and subsets using a visual representation to describe relationships between sets of rational numbers.
Yes. Any integer n can be written as n/1.

faq.q: What is the difference between natural and whole numbers?
faq.a: Whole numbers include 0; natural numbers start at 1.
No. π cannot be written as a fraction of integers. You will study such numbers in Grade 8.
